text: Got a letter you cannot understand? Do this.
Step one. Take a clear photo of it.
Step two. Ask the AI: explain this like I am a friend.
Step three. Ask: what do I need to do, and by when?

Tiny medicine print? Make AI read it for you.
One. Photograph the label.
Two. Ask: what does this say, in big simple words?
Three. Always confirm with your pharmacist.
Planning a trip? Let AI do the boring part.
One. Tell it where and for how many days.
Two. Add what you like. Slow walks, good food, no stairs.
Three. Ask for a day by day plan you can print.
Nothing for dinner? Try this in thirty seconds.
One. List what you already have.
Two. Say how long you have, and who is eating.
Three. Ask for one easy recipe. Then cook it.
This text says your bank account is locked. Do not tap it. Do this instead.
One. Do not tap the link. Just look at it.
Two. Paste the words into AI and ask: is this a scam?
Three. Call the number on your real card. Not the one in the text.
You need to write a thank you note and you are staring at a blank page. Fix it in two minutes.
One. Tell AI who it is for and why.
Two. Ask it to keep it warm, short and in your voice.
Three. Read it, change a word or two, and send it.
You have eight seconds before a scammer on the phone gets what they want. Say this sentence.
One. Say: I will call you back on the number I already have.
Two. Hang up. Do not wait for them to answer.
Three. Call the real number from your card or the official website.
The pharmacist said a word you did not catch. You nodded anyway. Fix it from the car.
One. Type the word, or take a photo of the paper.
Two. Ask: explain this like I am twelve, and what should I ask my doctor?
Three. Write down the three questions and call the pharmacist back.
Scam or safe? Four seconds each. Go.
Round one. A text says: your package is held. Tap this link to pay one dollar. Scam or safe?
Scam! Real carriers do not text you payment links.
Round two. Your pharmacy texts: your refill is ready. No link. Scam or safe?
Safe! No link, no payment, and it is from a number you know.
Not sure? Paste it into AI and ask: is this a scam?
One wrong tap and a scammer gets your money. Can you spot the scam?
Round one. A pop up says: your computer has a virus, call this number now. Scam or safe?
Scam! Close the window. Real warnings never give a phone number.
Round two. A friend texts: are we still on for lunch Thursday? Scam or safe?
Safe! Known friend, normal question, no link and no money.
Not sure? Ask AI before you click.
Scammers took over ten billion dollars from Americans in one year. Which of these texts is one of them?
Round one. A text says: you owe one dollar ninety nine for a package. Pay here. Scam or safe?
Scam! The one ninety nine is bait. They want your card number.
Round two. A text from your pharmacy: your prescription is ready. Reply C to confirm. Scam or safe?
Safe. No link, no payment, and it matches a number you already use.
Not sure? Paste it into AI and ask if it is a scam.
Scam or safe? Quick fire. Go.
Round one. Your grandson calls and says: I am in jail, send money, do not tell mom. Scam or safe?
Scam! Hang up and call him on his real number.
Round two. Your bank app shows a notice that you opened yourself. Scam or safe?
Safe! You opened it yourself, not through a link.
When in doubt, ask AI before you click.
This is what a bill can look like. Watch.
Now ask AI: say this in plain English. Done.
Paste any confusing paragraph, then ask: say this in plain English.
You nodded like you understood your test results. You did not. Watch this.
Ask AI to say it plainly. Your average blood sugar is a little high. Ask your doctor what to do next.
Ask the second question too: what should I ask my doctor?
Insurance letters are written to confuse. Watch this.
Ask AI to say it simply. They paid part. You owe the rest.
Always ask: what does this mean, and what do I do next?
You clicked agree without reading. Here is what you actually agreed to.
Ask AI for the short version. They can change or cancel it any time.
Paste the fine print. Ask: what should I watch out for?
The intern got promoted. He is twenty two. And he has been hiding one thing.
Everyone clapped. You clapped too. You have been here eleven years.
His secret? Every report, every email, every deadline. He asks an AI first.
He did not work harder than you. Nobody ever showed you. That is the only gap.
One live class, in plain English, with real people. It is not too late.
Free live AI classes in small groups. Rye side dot com.
This is the email that could get you a fourteen thousand dollar raise. Anyone can write it in two minutes.
A sixty one year old can do it. You tell AI your wins. It writes the email.
Most people never ask. Not because they do not deserve it. Because nobody taught them this.
It is a skill, like typing once was. And you can learn it live, in a small group.
Point of view. You find out your dentist's receptionist is not a person.
She booked you, checked your insurance, and said hope your day goes great. All a program.
It is in your phone, your bank, your doctor's office, your grandkids' homework. AI is everywhere.
Does that make you feel a little overwhelmed? That is normal. Nobody explained it to you.
It is not about being smart. It is one friendly class, in plain English.
Stop. Do not answer that call from your bank.
It sounds exactly like them. Same voice. Same hold music. A computer can copy a voice from a few seconds of audio.
If you answer, they say your account is hacked and ask you to move money. Hang up. Call the number on your card.
Scams are everywhere, and with AI, older folks are getting left behind. The defense is not luck. It is education.
Point of view. You are fifty eight, and you just found out you did not have to type any of this.
Thirty years of typing with one finger. And the mic on your keyboard was right there.
Tap the mic and talk. Then ask AI to make it sound polite. Done.
You are not slow. Nobody ever showed you. That is the whole gap.
That is not your grandson on the phone. A voice can be copied for almost nothing.
A few seconds of audio from a video is enough. It sounds exactly like family, and it is crying.
Here is the one thing that stops it. Pick a family safe word today. If they cannot say it, hang up.
Scams are everywhere, and with AI, older folks are getting left behind. The defense is education, not luck.
Your phone is letting scammers ring you all day, and there is one setting that stops it.
On an iPhone, open Settings, Phone, and turn on Silence Unknown Callers.
On Android, open your Phone app, tap Settings, and turn on Caller ID and spam protection.
Nobody shows you this stuff. It is not you. It is education, and it is free.
Point of view. Everyone in the meeting is using AI, and you are pretending to take notes.
They are not smarter than you. They typed one sentence and got a summary in four seconds.
Everyone under thirty got shown how. Nobody showed you. That is the whole gap.
One live class, in plain English, closes it. You are not behind. You are untaught.
